prompt:
Style references only: the attached images set the painting style, the colours and the mood. Do not copy their content. Paint it as a concept artist's painted sketch sheet for a cozy, bright strategy game: loose hand-painted brushwork with visible strokes, soft painted light from a warm sunny afternoon coming from the front right, cheerful bright colours, a warm light cream paper background with a soft painted shadow under each object. It is a painting, not a 3D render, not low poly, not a game screenshot. Cozy and friendly like a storybook toy, never grim. No people, no text, no labels, no numbers, no letters, no watermark.

The sheet shows three piles of rounded boulders for a toy fortress game, side by side in one row, each standing on its own square grass tile one metre wide, seen in a three-quarter view from slightly above. The tiles lie loose on the cream paper like game pieces, their edges drawn as a slightly darker green line, so the size of each pile reads against its tile. Every pile is chunky, smooth and stylized like toy stones in warm grey with cream highlights, about as wide as its tile and about two thirds of a tile tall, never sharp or angular. Left: two big rounded boulders leaning together, one slightly behind the other. Middle: one single large rounded boulder with a painted crack and a little moss on top. Right: a pyramid of three rounded stones, a big one below and two smaller ones on top. In front of the middle pile, on its own tile, stands a small dark iron cannon on a low square plate that fills its tile: it is the size reference of the game, and the boulders must read as clearly bigger than the cannon.
